visual.title: Eleven checks, three states, one clearance list
visual.description: A labelled sequence for building a counterparty vetting file whose output is a dated not-yet rather than an impression.
steps: Step 1, run the permission checks first: current registration in each state where the merchant or the offer sits, read as of a date, with the register's own record attached.
Step 2, test any programme claim against the published criteria for that programme rather than against a logo or a partner page, and record the result as verified, failed or unresolved.
Step 3, search the public enforcement and litigation record and convert each item found into a specific document check on the offer letter, the disbursement, the debit authority and the template.

Step 4, read the counterparty's own contract template through the four channels and mark the enforceable and unenforceable provisions, including any confession of judgment, forum or arbitration clause.
Step 5, tally the three states, treat unresolved as blocking, write the clearance list that would move each unresolved row, and close with an advisory note that alleges nothing and predicts nothing.

lessons.title: Capstone: assembling a deal packet an independent reviewer can audit in twenty minutes
lessons.explanation: The packet is eleven items in a fixed order, and the order is part of the design, because each item answers the question the next one assumes. Item 1 is the identity and scope block: the merchant, the governing jurisdiction, the date, the preparer and the preparer's own compensation, plus one sentence stating what the packet is not. Item 2 is the comparison sheet with its rows, its two denominators and its footnotes. Item 3 is the disclosure audit against the governing numbered list, with conditional rows marked as conditional. Item 4 is the clause read sorted into amount, timing, responsibility and enforceability. Item 5 is the public-record read with every filing dated, its collateral indication quoted and a not-proved column. Item 6 is the cash rebuild from the tax documents, with the reconciliation written as an equality and timing items listed separately. Item 7 is the evidence calendar with one row per period, five fields per row, statuses and the relied-upon version. Item 8 is the outreach record: the claim table, the required channel elements and the dated test of the opt-out mechanism. Item 9 is the counterparty vetting file with its three-state rows and clearance list. Item 10 is the assumptions log, in which every assumption carries its source and the fact that would falsify it. Item 11 is the decision line: what the evidence supports, the conditions, the reversal point and the decline path. Two standards are quoted rather than paraphrased. The SBA lending criteria section states that the applicant must be creditworthy, that loans must be so sound as to reasonably assure repayment, that Lenders and CDCs must use appropriate and prudent generally acceptable commercial credit analysis processes and procedures consistent with those used for their similarly sized, non-SBA guaranteed commercial loans, that Lenders, CDCs and SBA may use a business credit scoring model, and the criteria that may be considered when approving direct or guaranteed loans. That is five sentences, and the packet states the count and the amendment because a packet that misstates its own standard fails the audit it was assembled for. The second borrowed idea is named as borrowed: the OCC's Rating Credit Risk handbook, which governs bank credit risk rating systems and not advisors, says that the essential test of a good write-up is whether it supports the rating, and its informal rule is that if in doubt, you write it up. The packet borrows the reasoning, states the source, and states the scope.
lessons.example: An independent reviewer who has never read the file runs the same three tests on each of the eleven items: can I find the source document, can I reproduce the arithmetic, and can I identify what would reverse the conclusion? Eleven items times three tests is thirty-three cells, and the first pass answers twenty-nine of them in just under twenty minutes, which is 1.82 minutes per item. Four gaps are named rather than argued about: two duplicated statement months have no relied-upon version line, one percentage on the comparison sheet names no denominator, and the decision line has no reversal condition. The comparison sheet's error illustrates why the reviewer's second test matters. The first version of the sheet computed net proceeds as $57,300 by omitting the $895 administrative fee, which produced a cost of $141.36 per $100 of net proceeds; itemising the fee gives net proceeds of $56,405.00 and $143.60 per $100, so the omitted fee understated the measure by $2.24 per $100 and was caught only because the reviewer could not reproduce the figure from the documents in the packet. Two hostile objections arrive and both are answered from the packet rather than from memory. The first is that the cash rebuild ignores the $58,000 of December receipts collected in January; the answer is that the rebuild starts from net profit as the return reports it, on the cash method, and the $58,000 is listed in the timing row, with the reconciliation from $412,000 of receipts to $468,000 of deposits shown as an equality. The second is that presenting $143.60 per $100 of net proceeds beside $124.81 for a term loan quietly recommends the loan; the answer is that the sheet has no winner column, that the two instruments are priced on different bases, and that the packet states both the cost difference and the contribution difference, 25.12 percent of monthly contribution against 2.85 percent, so the reader sees the trade rather than a ranking. After the four gaps are closed, the reviewer's second pass answers thirty-three of thirty-three cells. The packet closes with three lines it is not allowed to omit: the preparer's compensation, the statement that nothing in it is a legal opinion or a prediction of any funder's decision, and the date on which the checks were run.
lessons.question: A reviewer asks why the packet puts the disclosure audit before the decision line, since the decision is the point. What is the correct answer?
lessons.answer: Because each item answers a question the next one assumes: a decision line written before the disclosure audit will not carry the conditional rows the audit produces, and a reversal point written before the clause read will not name the clause that changes the answer, so reordering the packet converts checkable findings into assertions.
lessons.distractor: The order is conventional and does not affect the content, since a reader can move between items at will and the decision line is the only item that requires agreement.
lessons.correction: The order is a control, not a convention. The comparison sheet produces the denominators the cost conversation needs; the disclosure audit produces the conditional rows that must be carried as conditions rather than as defects; the clause read produces the reversal candidates; the record read and the cash rebuild produce the two facts a decision can be reversed by; and the calendar, the outreach record and the vetting file produce the conditions in the decision line. Written in that sequence the decision line is a summary of findings; written out of sequence it is a conclusion that has to be defended item by item, and the reviewer's three tests then fail on the arithmetic rather than on the judgement.

depth.definitions: A packet is a fixed-order set of artifacts with one decision line, built so that a reader without the advisor's context can audit it. The assumptions log lists each assumption, its source and the observation that would falsify it. A reversal point is the specific fact or measurement at which the recommendation would change, stated in advance and in the documents' own units. A decline path names the case in which the answer is no and what the merchant would do instead, so that a no is a work product rather than an absence of one. The reviewer's three tests are source, arithmetic and reversal, and the completeness count is the number of items multiplied by three: eleven items, thirty-three cells. Borrowed reasoning is material from a regime that does not bind the reader, quoted with its source and its scope, used for the logic and never for authority. The amending citation belongs to the standard: the lending criteria section as amended by 88 FR 21085 has five sentences, and the fourth permits a business credit scoring model. Scope statements are part of the definitions rather than a disclaimer: nothing in a packet is legal advice, a credit decision, a promise of funding, or a certification of professional competence.
depth.mechanism: Four mechanisms give the packet its force. The first is sequence: each item presupposes the previous one, so the order makes gaps visible as breaks in a chain rather than as disagreements about judgement. The second is the reviewer's independence: because the tests are mechanical and the documents are named with dates, a reader who distrusts the advisor entirely can still complete the audit, which is the property that separates an audit object from a persuasion object. The third is falsifiability: naming a reversal point converts a disagreement into a test, so a reviewer who thinks the trough is deeper has something to compute rather than something to assert. The fourth is the scope discipline of borrowed standards: citing a bank supervisory handbook while stating that it binds banks and not advisors transfers the reasoning without claiming authority, and misstating the standard's own text, as by describing a five-sentence section as four sentences or omitting the sentence that permits a credit scoring model, destroys the packet's credibility at the one point where a reviewer is most likely to check. The packet is therefore complete not when it answers the merchant's question but when it survives three mechanical tests per item.
depth.secondExample: The same eleven items assembled for a not-yet answer look different in only three places, and the difference shows what the packet is for. Item 3's conditional rows are joined by unresolved rows from the vetting file, item 11 becomes a clearance list with an owner and a date for each item rather than a recommendation, and the assumptions log gains a line for each unknown with the document that would resolve it. Assembled for a decline, item 11 states the disqualifying fact in the documents' own terms, names what would change it, and records what the merchant was told and when, which keeps the decline useful rather than merely final. In both variants the ten preceding items are unchanged, which is the test of whether the artifacts were built as evidence or as argument: they survive a different conclusion without being rewritten. A packet whose first ten items had to change when the answer changed was a brief for a conclusion rather than a file.
depth.mistake: The recurring failures are five. Building the packet as persuasion: adjectives where documents belong, and a decision line whose reversal point is unstated. Omitting the preparer's compensation, which is the line every reviewer of an advisor's work looks for first. Reporting percentages whose base is unstated, which is how a factor of 1.35 becomes 143.60 per $100 of net proceeds becomes 25.12 percent of contribution without any of the three being wrong. Quoting a standard from a paraphrase, which in this level's own subject means describing the lending criteria section as four sentences and dropping the sentence that permits a business credit scoring model. And claiming authority for borrowed supervisory reasoning, which turns a defensible packet into an overstated one. The diagnostic is the thirty-three-cell count: if a reviewer cannot answer source, arithmetic and reversal for an item, that item is a draft, and if the packet claims a scope it does not have, the audit stops there.
depth.application: Capstone task. Assemble the eleven items for one file, then have a person who has not seen the file run the three tests per item and count the cells they can answer. Model response: a packet containing the scope block with the preparer's compensation; the comparison sheet showing $81,000.00 of total repayment, $56,405.00 of net proceeds, $143.60 per $100 of net proceeds and 25.12 percent of monthly contribution, with the omitted-fee error corrected from $141.36; the disclosure audit with eight origination items scored and the conditional row left open; the clause read across four channels; the record read with three dated filings, one lapse and a not-proved column; the cash rebuild from $412,000 of receipts and $96,400 of net profit to $800.00 of free cash with the $58,000 timing item separated; the evidence calendar at sixty cells with nine current, one stale and two missing; the outreach record with five of fourteen claims deleted and the opt-out mechanism tested on day thirty-one; the vetting file at four verified, three failed and four unresolved, 63.64 percent blocking, with a clearance list; the assumptions log with falsifiers; and a decision line naming the reversal point and the decline path. Rubric: four points for all eleven items present in order; four for the thirty-three-cell audit with every unanswered cell named; two for the compensation, scope and date lines; two for stating the standard's sentence count and the borrowed handbook's scope correctly; two for a reversal point expressed in the documents' units. A packet missing the compensation line, misstating the standard, or ending in a conclusion with no reversal point cannot pass.
depth.summary: The packet is the level's whole output in one object: evidence first, in a fixed order, audited by three mechanical tests per item, and closed with a decision line that names its own reversal condition. Its standards are quoted with their counts and their scopes, its borrowed reasoning is labelled as borrowed, and its limitations are on the page rather than in the advisor's head. What it never becomes is a promise, a legal opinion or a certification, and what it always is, is checkable by someone who does not trust its author.

visual.title: The eleven-item packet in sequence, audited by thirty-three cells
visual.description: A labelled assembly and audit sequence that turns the level's artifacts into one object a sceptical reader can verify without the author.
steps: Step 1, write the scope block first, with merchant, jurisdiction, date, preparer, the preparer's compensation, and one sentence saying what the packet is not.
Step 2, stack the evidence items in dependency order: comparison sheet, disclosure audit, clause read, record read, cash rebuild, evidence calendar, outreach record, vetting file.
Step 3, write the assumptions log with a source and a falsifier per assumption, then derive the decision line from the items above it rather than from the conclusion you already hold.
Step 4, run the reviewer's three tests on each of the eleven items, source, arithmetic and reversal, and count the answered cells out of thirty-three.
Step 5, close with the scope, compensation and date lines, and state the standard's sentence count and the borrowed handbook's scope so a reviewer checks the right text.

questions.prompt: You inherit an outreach email whose second sentence offers 'an SBA-backed advance with approval guaranteed in 24 hours' and whose footer has an unsubscribe link. The merchant list was bought from a vendor. Write the decisions and the tests.
questions.answer: Delete the affiliation and the guaranteed approval, since neither can be supported by a document and both are the claims this course prohibits; verify and test the footer rather than assuming it, because the opt-out mechanism must remain capable of receiving requests for no less than 30 days after transmission; check the list against suppression before sending; and read the channel rules for the technology actually used, which for calls or texts to mobile numbers imposes a prior express written consent standard rather than an opt-out line.
questions.distractor: Keep both claims but add a disclaimer that approval is subject to underwriting, and rely on the vendor's warranty that the list was lawfully collected, since the vendor is the sender's compliance provider.
questions.correction: A disclaimer does not cure a claim that implies a government connection or promises an outcome; the claim table's test is whether a document with a date supports the sentence, and no document supports either one. The unsubscribe link needs evidence, not assumption: it must remain capable for at least thirty days and requests must be honoured within ten business days, so the record shows a click-through test on a later date. Suppression is the sender's duty even when a list was purchased, and an opt-out line is not the required element for every channel, because the texting provisions turn on consent rather than on an unsubscribe mechanism.

questions.prompt: A vetting file for a funder shows four unresolved checks, one failed check on the funder's own contract template, and a current registration. The funder's representative says the failed item is 'standard language everyone uses'. What is the output and the note?
questions.answer: Not yet: unresolved blocks exactly as a fail blocks, so seven items block the file; the note records the specific template findings, what each unresolved row needs to clear it, and states plainly that the file does not allege dishonesty or predict an outcome, and that registration is read as of a date because it can lapse.
questions.distractor: Yes with a caveat, because the registration is current, the failed item is common in the market, and the merchant can rely on the clause being unenforceable in the state where the contract sits.
questions.correction: Market practice is not a vetting result, and the fact that a clause is unenforceable in one state does not make it harmless: it deters a challenge, which is the effect the prohibition was written to remove. The honest output names the findings in the documents' own terms, converts each unresolved row into a document request with a date, and keeps the advisory note free of character claims and predictions. The alternative is that the merchant discovers the clause, the undisclosed fee and the missing disclosure item after signature, when leverage has moved.

questions.prompt: A colleague hands you a packet with a decision line on page one, a comparison sheet without footnotes, and no assumptions log, and asks you to review it in ten minutes. Write the review.
questions.answer: Return it unfinished: the decision line has been written before the evidence items that would qualify it, the sheet's missing footnotes remove the denominators and the timing assumptions a reader needs to reproduce the arithmetic, and the absent assumptions log leaves the falsifiers unstated, so the reviewer's three tests cannot be answered for most items.
questions.distractor: Approve it with a note that the order is unusual, since the arithmetic in the sheet appears internally consistent and the decision line is the part the merchant will read anyway.
questions.correction: The packet's order is a control: each item answers the question the next one assumes, and a decision line written first cannot carry the conditional rows, reversal candidates or clearance items that the evidence items produce. Footnotes are where the denominators, the timing assumptions and the preparer's compensation live, and without them the sheet is unreproducible. The assumptions log is what makes the conclusion falsifiable, and the reviewer's three tests, source, arithmetic and reversal, are exactly what a ten-minute review is for.

questions.prompt: Two funders quote the same merchant. Funder one's disclosure lists nine numbered items and includes the broker-compensation line; funder two's document lists six and includes an annualized rate. The merchant asks which document is more honest. Answer him.
questions.answer: Neither: the lists belong to different jurisdictions and different policy choices, so the honest comparison is which items the governing regime for this merchant requires and whether each document carries them, plus whether the conditional rows are marked, rather than a ranking of documents by length.
questions.distractor: Funder one's document is more complete because nine items cover more than six, so the merchant should treat the shorter document as less transparent and press for the missing items.
questions.correction: Counting items across different statutes is not a measure of honesty, because the lists are not translations of one another: across the pair used in this level the two statutes produce fifteen item slots describing eleven distinct requirements, of which three are exact counterparts and two appear in only one list. The correct task is to identify the governing list for this merchant's jurisdiction, mark the conditional rows, score presence, error and absence per row, and then say separately whether either document's arithmetic reconciles. An annualized-rate item is not an APR, and no factor is converted into one on the merchant's behalf.

questions.prompt: A merchant's file contains a financeable offer, a clean vetting file, and one clause in the contract requiring disputes to be heard 1,150 miles away, with two witnesses needed. Before presenting the file, what does the packet include on that point, and why?
questions.answer: A clause row in the packet stating the clause's own words, the fact that the governing state's law makes an out-of-state forum clause unenforceable and that face-to-face arbitration outside the recipient's jurisdiction cannot be required, the provider paying the arbitrators' costs, and a price for the risk of not raising it, using the computed $2,790.00 of travel and business time.
questions.distractor: A note that the clause is unenforceable, so no further action is needed, since a provision that cannot be enforced in the state is not a risk the merchant carries.
questions.correction: Unenforceability changes who wins in theory, not what the merchant spends to contest the point, and the packet prices that: two witnesses at $620 airfare, two nights at $185, $120 of ground transport, plus six hours at $95 comes to $2,790.00. The clause row also belongs in the four-channel sort, since a forum clause moves responsibility rather than amount, and the reversal condition follows from it: the recommendation would change if the merchant, on counsel's advice, must treat an out-of-state proceeding as a live cost.

questions.prompt: A merchant in one state is offered a fixed-payment advance with a reconciliation clause. Write the two reads the packet needs: the disclosure audit and the clause read, naming what each produces for the other.
questions.answer: The disclosure audit produces the item rows for the governing list, with the conditional prepayment row left open and the estimated-payments row scored, while the clause read produces the reconciliation clause's effect on the tail, so the audit's estimated number of payments and the clause's range describe the same uncertainty from two directions.
questions.distractor: The audit confirms the document is complete, and the clause read confirms the term, so the packet can state the completion date as a single number once the two have been checked.
questions.correction: A true-up mechanism keeps the remittance fixed while adjusting it to a percentage of sales or revenue, so the tail is a range and the disclosure's estimated number of payments is an estimate by the statute's own wording. Reading the two together is what prevents a packet from asserting a completion date that the instrument does not have, and it keeps the conditional disclosure row open rather than marking it as a defect.

questions.prompt: A search shows an all-assets filing from seven years ago with no continuation, and the tax return shows $96,400 of net profit against deposits of $468,000 with a cash method declared. Write the two findings and the one thing the packet must not conclude.
questions.answer: The filing's five-year effectiveness expired and, absent a continuation filed within the six months before that date, the security interest lapsed and is deemed never perfected as against a purchaser for value, while the return reconciles exactly at $412,000 of receipts plus $40,000 plus $9,500 plus $6,500 to $468,000 of deposits and rebuilds to $800.00 of free cash; the packet must not conclude either that the business is unencumbered or that the obligation is extinguished, because both are separate questions the documents do not answer.
questions.distractor: The filing is void and the business is unencumbered, so the packet can treat the position as first and the free-cash figure as capacity for a new remittance.
questions.correction: A lapse is a perfection fact and the debt is a separate fact; a search answers a narrow question. Likewise $800.00 of free cash is not a capacity number for a new obligation on its own, because the merchant's own drawings, debt service and reserves are decisions rather than constants. The packet's job is to state each finding with its date and its source, and to put the open questions in the not-proved column instead of resolving them by implication.

questions.prompt: A funder declines the requested amount and offers a smaller sum on a shorter tail at a higher factor, and the merchant asks whether he has been declined. Write the three-part answer.
questions.answer: Describe the counteroffer on three axes, amount, duration and cost per dollar of net proceeds, noting for the worked pair that it is 29.41 percent smaller, 16.67 percent shorter and 6.16 percent more expensive per dollar; state the regulatory position, that a refusal in substantially the amount or terms requested is adverse action unless the creditor makes a counteroffer and the applicant uses or expressly accepts the credit offered; and give the merchant the conditions list, including a dated payoff figure for existing obligations, because no funds have moved.
questions.distractor: Tell the merchant he has been declined, send the adverse action notice with reasons, and restart the search at a higher amount, since the funder reduced the request and the file should record the decline.
questions.correction: Whether the file is a decline depends on one fact the merchant controls, acceptance or refusal, and the regulation carves out an accepted counteroffer from the definition. Reporting it as a decline misstates the file and can produce a notice the definition does not require. The commercial read matters just as much: a smaller and shorter counteroffer that costs more per dollar of net proceeds is not simply a worse offer, because the tail and the contribution share move too, and a 33.39 percent share of weekly contribution against 37.13 percent is the fact the merchant will feel.

questions.prompt: A comparison sheet reports net proceeds of $57,300 for a $60,000 advance with a 1.35 factor over 26 weeks, and the contract shows a $2,700 origination fee and an $895 administrative fee. Correct the sheet and state why the error mattered.
questions.answer: Net proceeds are $60,000 minus $2,700 minus $895, which is $56,405.00, so total repayment of $81,000.00 is $143.60 per $100 of net proceeds rather than the $141.36 reported; the omitted $895 understated the measure by $2.24 per $100, and the error was visible only because the reviewer could not reproduce the figure from the documents.
questions.distractor: Net proceeds of $57,300 is close enough for a comparison since the $895 is administrative, and the sheet can note the fee in a footnote rather than in the denominator, because the merchant will pay it either way.
questions.correction: Every fee deducted or withheld at disbursement belongs in net proceeds, because net proceeds is the denominator that tells the merchant what the money costs per dollar actually received. A fee moved to a footnote flatters the measure and cannot be caught later. The sheet's second reviewer test exists for this: a figure that cannot be reproduced from dated documents with a calculator is not a figure the packet may carry.

questions.prompt: An evidence calendar shows eleven statement months current, one month stale by 264 days, and one month with no row content. The merchant says the set is complete because every month is accounted for. Correct him and state the consequence.
questions.answer: A stale month and a missing month are different facts with different consequences: the stale row shows the business traded and the evidence is outside its window, while the missing row means nothing is known about that period, and the missing row blocks the file while the stale row is context rather than current evidence; the log records each per period with its five fields so the two are never averaged.
questions.distractor: Both are minor documentation gaps on one of twelve periods, so the set can proceed while the two months are refreshed, since the other eleven months establish the pattern.
questions.correction: Because the calendar records periods rather than a total, the gaps are countable, and the missing period is the one that matters: a lender or reviewer asks which period is absent, not what proportion arrived. Leaving the stale row marked as current would overstate the file, and a summary row reading eleven of twelve would destroy the distinction entirely. The cost of collecting the missing month is also quantified, which is what makes the schedule persuasive rather than merely firm.

questions.prompt: An outreach draft contains fourteen checkable claims, five of which have no supporting document, an unsubscribe link built yesterday, and a list of 480 addresses. Write the corrections, the tests and the honest volume statement.
questions.answer: Delete the five unsupported claims, rewrite the ones that can be sourced, leave the nine re-checked claims, test the unsubscribe mechanism again after the thirty-day threshold because it must remain capable of receiving requests for no less than 30 days and requests must be honoured within 10 business days, check the 480 addresses against the suppression list with its date, and state reply rates as observations from a named batch size, such as 10.08 and 7.68 responses per 480 depending on the rate.
questions.distractor: Keep the fourteen claims but soften the five, since a hedged claim is unlikely to mislead, and rely on the new unsubscribe link because it was tested when it was built.
questions.correction: A hedged claim without a document still fails the substantiation requirement, and the test is whether evidence is in hand rather than whether the wording is cautious. A mechanism tested on the day it was built has not been tested against the provision that requires it to remain capable for thirty days after each transmission. And a reply rate presented as an expectation rather than as an observation from a stated batch is a prediction the artifact is not entitled to make.

questions.prompt: A vetting file has eleven checks with four verified, three failed and four unresolved, including an unconfirmed registration and a contract template containing a confession of judgment provision. Write the output, the clearance list and the boundary on what the file may say.
questions.answer: The output is not yet, because unresolved blocks exactly as a fail blocks, so seven of eleven checks block the file at 63.64 percent; the clearance list names the confirmation of current registration, the disclosure survey of the governing item list, the two references and the signer's authority; and the file may state what was verified and what failed against the documents in hand but may not allege dishonesty or predict the outcome of any transaction.
questions.distractor: The output is yes with conditions, since four checks cleared, the failures are documentary and a confession of judgment provision is unenforceable in the state where the contract sits.
questions.correction: Registration is a dated permission rather than a permanent quality, so an unconfirmed registration is exactly the row that should block; a confession of judgment provision is a finding about the document regardless of its enforceability, because its practical effect is to deter a challenge; and the three-state rule exists so that ignorance is not routed into approval. The file's value is that it converts an unknown counterparty into a list of documents that would change the answer, which is what the merchant needs before signing rather than after.

questions.prompt: A packet reaches its decision line and names no reversal point. The reviewer's three tests are source, arithmetic and reversal. Write the review and the fix.
questions.answer: The packet is unfinished, because an item that cannot answer what would reverse it has no falsifier and the review stops there; the fix is to state the reversal in the documents' own units, for example the weekly contribution level at which the remittance share breaches the limit the packet assumed, and to add the matching line to the assumptions log with the observation that would falsify it.
questions.distractor: The decision line is the conclusion and the reversal point is optional, since the merchant wants an answer rather than a list of conditions under which the answer changes.
questions.correction: A recommendation with no reversal condition cannot be disagreed with on evidence, only on opinion, which is why the reversal point is the mechanism that converts a dispute into a computation. It also disciplines the advisor: a reversal stated in advance prevents a conclusion from being revised silently when facts move, and it forces the assumption behind the conclusion to be visible with its falsifier in the log.

questions.prompt: A merchant insists on signing today because the seller's quote expires, while the file has one missing statement month, a fee in the offer summary that the contract does not carry, and an unconfirmed registration. Write what the advisor presents and refuses.
questions.answer: Present a not-yet with three dated conditions and a clearance list, state the fee discrepancy in both documents' own numbers, and refuse to describe any funder's decision or to sign off on the discrepancy; the seller's deadline is a fact about the seller's quote and not a fact about the file, and the merchant's decision remains the merchant's to make with the conditions written down.
questions.distractor: Present the file as ready with the three items flagged as administrative, since the merchant accepts the risk, the quote deadline is real, and the fee difference is small.
questions.correction: Flagging a known fee discrepancy as administrative is how a hidden cost reaches a merchant's signature; the contract and the summary must be reconciled or the difference stated in dollars before anything else happens. Pressure, including a real deadline, is handled by naming what the file supports and what it does not, not by inventing urgency in the other direction or by softening a finding. The advisor's refusal is narrow: no prediction, no approval, no sign-off on a discrepancy.

questions.prompt: A reviewer objects that the packet's comparison sheet shows the advance at $143.60 per $100 of net proceeds against a term loan at $124.81, and concludes the packet is recommending the advance. Answer the objection.
questions.answer: The sheet has no winner column and the two instruments are priced on different bases, so both rows are presented with their denominators, tails and contribution shares, 25.12 percent of monthly contribution for the advance against 2.85 percent for the loan, and the packet states the cost difference of $18.79 per $100 and the tail difference of roughly six months against 48 months without ranking them.
questions.distractor: Add a recommendation line naming the loan, since the per-$100 measure is the fairest basis of comparison and the packet should be decisive when the arithmetic is clear.
questions.correction: A purchase of receivables priced by a factor and an amortising loan priced by a nominal rate are not made commensurable by any arithmetic the advisor is permitted to perform, and converting one into the other's terms is precisely what the course prohibits. The packet's contribution is to make both facts legible, the higher cost per dollar and the much shorter tail, with the cadence converted to the same period, and to leave the working-capital decision with the merchant whose cash flow it is.

questions.prompt: Write the four sentences a packet's scope block must carry about its own standards and limits, and explain the counting rule that makes one of them checkable.
questions.answer: It states the standard it measures the file against and counts that standard's sentences, five in the lending criteria section as amended by 88 FR 21085, with the fourth permitting Lenders, CDCs and SBA to use a business credit scoring model; it names borrowed supervisory reasoning and states that it binds banks rather than advisors; it states the preparer's compensation; and it states that nothing in the packet is a legal opinion, a credit decision, a promise of funding or a certification of competence.
questions.distractor: It states that the file meets SBA standards, that the analysis follows published supervisory guidance, and that the merchant's application is strong, with the compensation disclosed on request.
questions.correction: Claiming that a file meets a standard the advisor does not administer is an overstatement, and describing a bank supervisory handbook as governing a broker's analysis imports authority the document does not carry. Counting the standard's provisions is the check that keeps the summary honest: a packet that describes a five-sentence section as having four sentences, and drops the sentence permitting a credit scoring model, can be caught by any reader with the current text, which is exactly the test the packet invites.

questions.prompt: Cumulative capstone. A merchant's file contains an offer with a reconciliation clause, a contract whose prepayment clause is silent, a search showing a lapsed all-assets filing, a cash-method return, a calendar missing one month, an outreach record, and a vetting file with two unresolved rows. Write the packet's decision line and its four conditions.
questions.answer: The decision line reads not yet, with the four conditions: a refreshed payoff figure and the missing statement month cleared, with each carrying a date; the silent prepayment clause read to the merchant in its own terms so no unearned saving is implied; the lapsed filing and the two unresolved vetting rows listed as open questions with the documents that would resolve them; and the reversal point stated in the documents' units, such as the weekly contribution level at which the remittance share under the reconciliation clause breaches the limit the packet assumed.
questions.distractor: The decision line reads yes, since the offer is financeable and most items clear, with the lapsed filing noted as an advantage, the missing month and unresolved rows carried as routine follow-ups, and the prepayment question left to closing.
questions.correction: Each of the four items is a fact rather than a formality: a lapsed filing is a perfection fact that says nothing about the obligation, a missing statement month is a period about which nothing is known, an unresolved vetting row blocks like a fail, and a silent prepayment clause is what a merchant will misread unless it is stated plainly. A decision line that carries four conditions is more useful than a yes with four footnotes, because the conditions are the merchant's work list and the reviewer's checklist, and neither predicts a funder's decision.
